_meta.description:
Lane Cove social-graph priors — declarative rules that turn a sampled population into a partial 'who-knew-whom-on-day-0' graph. Without these the SocialGraphService starts empty (every pair = stranger). With these, agents have realistic pre-existing ties: same-household roommates / family, same-ethnic-enclave acquaintances, same-commute-pattern peers, same-archetype-similar-age weak ties.

Each rule produces a target encounter_count for matched pairs; the SocialGraphService.preload_ties() converts these into Tie records with strength = N/(N+K) using the standard formula.
calibration_notes: Rules are calibrated to give average ~5-8 ties per agent at day 0
encounter_count_seed values are 'as if N encounters had already happened' — they map to strength via N/(N+10)
pair_cap_per_agent prevents one agent from getting 100+ priors when the rule matches widely
ethnicity_enclave is intentionally limited to non-Australia ethnicities to model migrant network effects

rules.comment: Same home_location → roommate / family. Strong tie (strength ≈ 0.86).
Same non-anglo country-of-birth + recent arrival → migrant enclave acquaintance. Weak tie (~0.29).
Same archetype + age within 8 years → 'people like me'. Weak tie (~0.23).
Same daily commute pattern → bus / tunnel familiar face. Very weak tie (~0.17).
Volunteer status → bushcare / theatre / library volunteer overlap. Weak tie (~0.33).
Both have school-age kids + heavy childcare → school gate / mothers group peer. Weak tie (~0.23).
